subject: Immediate decision: traffic curtailment & canary revert for model v14s latency deviation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: sre@datacompany.com
Date: 2028-05-12T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Elevated p95 for model v14s in us-west -- proposal for immediate mitigation

Team —

Monitoring alerted at 08:55 PT to a sustained p95 jump for model v14s serving DataCorp (traffic routed from us-west-primary). Baseline p95 historically ~750ms; across the last 30m we've seen ~2.9s p95 (1.2s -> 2.9s over 20m). Error rates (4xx/5xx) are unchanged. Throughput is steady.

Quick data:
- Window: 08:40–09:10 PT
- p50: 220ms -> 240ms
- p95: 1.2s -> 2.9s
- tail (99th): 4.1s
- QPS: 360 (no significant drop)

Attached perf snapshot with sample traces and kernel timings. Early triage (local repro on staging with same config) suggests increased KV cache misses and kernel fallback on one memory-bound path for sequence lengths >1024.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked by speed & impact):
1) Traffic curtailment: cap requests to DataCorp to 75% of current QPS on v14s and route remainder to v12-stable (compatible signature) — low-risk but may increase cost and slightly change response characteristics.
2) Canary revert: revert v14s canary group to previous build (v14r) — expected return to baseline latency within ~5–8 minutes; requires authorization for rollback on a customer SLA (DataCorp).
3) Progressive quantization rollback/compile tweak: not instant; multi-hour fix.

Requesting authorization to proceed with option 1 immediately and option 2 as follow-on if metrics don't improve in 30 minutes. This will affect the SLA for DataCorp; they are on a standard enterprise uptime/latency commitment. If we need to do a canary revert, we should notify the account and get ops acknowledgement.

Attachments: perf_snapshot_v14s-20280512.csv

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated p95 for model v14s in us-west -- proposal for immediate mitigation

Ben / Karthik —

Thanks for the signal. Quick clarifying Qs before I greenlight anything that touches production traffic:
- What's the expected customer-visible delta if we cap traffic to 75%? (latency & any degraded tokens)
- If we do a canary revert (v14r), what rollback window & re-compile risks are there?

If this is primarily KV cache misses on a single kernel path, cap-first + route seems reasonable. I prefer cap now, then canary revert if metrics don't normalize within two 15-minute windows.

Karthik, can you confirm the runbook step list and blast radius? cc Marissa for account implications.

— Markus
Director, Production Reliability
markus_klein@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Elevated p95 for model v14s in us-west -- proposal for immediate mitigation

Folks —

Account note: DataCorp is on an Annual Enterprise SLA (latency commitments + financial credits defined). ARR with us is ~$320k; they run critical user workflows during our US business hours. Any visible degradation longer than 15 minutes will trigger formal remediation per contract.

I support Markus' approach: authorize traffic cap immediately, notify DataCorp of the mitigation and intent to canary revert if no improvement in 30m. If we do revert, recommend we proactively offer a one-off 10% service credit for any SLA shortfall >30m as a gesture (we can finalize with finance later).

Ben, please loop Elaine (DataCorp) with a short notice and give them the expected timeline and impact. Make sure SRE is aware and that the rollback runbook is attached.

Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated p95 for model v14s in us-west -- proposal for immediate mitigation

Markus / team —

Runbook & blast-radius: confirmed. Short summary:
- Traffic cap to 75% on v14s routed to v12-stable: config change via routing-policy; ~30s to take effect; no data loss; expected customer-visible token differences are minimal for most prompt shapes (compatibility validated).
- Canary revert to v14r: automated rollback job exists in ops-runbook (rollback_runbook_v14s.pdf). Revert steps: drain 10% canary, flip canary build, validate key traces for 2m, then scale to 100% if green. Estimated reversion time to 100%: ~6 minutes (includes validation).
- Risk: If the cause is correlated to hardware (specific GPU family in us-west racks), a revert may not fully resolve. We'll monitor kernel-level metrics and have fallback to route to eu-west if needed.

I authorize option 1 now and will initiate the canary revert if p95 does not improve to <1s within two 15-minute checks. I'll attach the runbook and start the routing change.

Attachments: rollback_runbook_v14s.pdf

Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Platform Reliability
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: 2028-05-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Notice: brief traffic curtailment + potential canary revert for v14s (DataCorp)

Elaine —

Quick heads-up from Redwood: our monitoring detected a latency increase on the v14s model serving your US traffic starting ~08:40 PT. We are immediately applying a targeted traffic cap (routing 25% of your qps away from v14s to our stable v12 variant) to reduce tail latency while we validate the underlying cause. This mitigation is in effect now and should be transparent to most users; you may notice slightly different output characteristics for in-flight requests routed to v12.

If we do not see p95 return to baseline (<1s) within the next 30–45 minutes, our engineering team will initiate a canary revert of v14s to the previous build (v14r). The revert is expected to complete within ~6 minutes and we will validate traces before scaling.

We want to be transparent: because you are on an enterprise SLA, an action like a revert is considered a configuration change that we notify you about. If the issue persists beyond 30 minutes, we also expect to offer a one-off 10% service credit for SLA shortfalls >30m as a good-faith gesture; we will finalize with your finance contacts if that becomes necessary.

Attachments: rollback_runbook_v14s.pdf, sla_mau_agreement_datacorp_2027.pdf

I will keep you posted with updates every 15 minutes until the situation stabilizes. Please reply here if you have any constraints on a canary revert in the next hour.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
